description: Three rows below Supports, one at each of the template's three words under it — 1.4.4 Does Not Support, 2.4.7 Not Evaluated, 4.1.2 Partially Supports — on three findings the case opens, one of them cited by two rows. The count is three, in the plural; the rows are listed in the standard's order; and the three owners are named once each, in the plan's order — 9.8, 9.9, 9.75 — which is neither the order the rows cite them in (9.9, 9.75, 9.8) nor the string's (9.75, 9.8, 9.9). A rule that counted one of the three words and not the other two, or named the first finding and stopped, or named a shared finding twice, or sorted the findings as strings, would read like a report with two rows fewer or one owner more.
